rules.title: Subtyping refines kind-equality with lifetime variance
rules.statement: sub <: sup holds when a value of type sub may be used where sup is expected. Subtyping augments lifetime-erased kind/structural compatibility with lifetime-aware variance constraints; it returns true for any cross-kind pair (leaving legitimate cross-kind coercions, e.g. IntLit→i32, &mut→&, Vec→slice, to the separate compatibility check) and only fails when sub and sup share a kind that has a variance rule and their lifetime-aware structure disagrees.

rules.title: &'a T is covariant in lifetime and pointee
rules.statement: For shared references: &'a T <: &'b U iff 'a: 'b (covariant lifetime) and T <: U (covariant pointee).

rules.title: &mut 'a T is covariant in lifetime, invariant in pointee
rules.statement: For mutable references: &'a mut T <: &'b mut U iff 'a: 'b (covariant lifetime) and T == U with lifetimes (invariant pointee). Hence &mut &'static T is NOT a subtype of &mut &'a T.

rules.title: *const covariant, *mut invariant; mut/const mismatch is shape diff
rules.statement: Raw pointers carry no lifetime. *const T is covariant in pointee (*const T <: *const U iff T <: U); *mut T is invariant in pointee (*mut T <: *mut U iff T == U with lifetimes). A const-vs-mut pointer-kind mismatch is a shape difference, deferred to the compatibility check (subtype returns true).

rules.title: Tuples covariant per element; arrays and slices covariant in element
rules.statement: (S0,..,Sn) <: (P0,..,Pn) iff each Si <: Pi (same arity). [T; N] and [T] are covariant in element type: sub <: sup iff elem(sub) <: elem(sup). Arity/shape mismatch is deferred to the compatibility check.

rules.title: Struct variance from per-def table keyed by package+name, default covariant
rules.statement: For same struct (matching pkg_name+struct_name), each type-arg position i and lifetime-arg position i is checked at its variance looked up from the per-definition variance table (key 'pkg.Name', subkeys '#i' for type args, '@i' for lifetime args). Absent table or absent entry defaults to covariant (Co). Differing struct name, package, or arg-list arity is a shape difference (subtype returns true).
rules.uncertainty: Variance table is user/compiler-supplied; this unit only consumes it.

rules.title: Enums covariant in all type-arg and lifetime-arg positions
rules.statement: For same enum (matching pkg_name+enum_name), every type-arg and lifetime-arg position is treated as covariant (Co); there is no per-enum variance table. Matches the covariant shape of Option/Result/Box. Differing name, package, or arity is a shape difference.
rules.uncertainty: Per-enum variance table not yet wired; Co is a conservative fallback (B81 compiler tag).

rules.title: Function pointers and closures: contravariant params, covariant return
rules.statement: FnPtr and Closure subtype identically: sub <: sup iff each param position is contravariant (sup_param <: sub_param) and the return type is covariant (sub_ret <: sup_ret), with matching param arity. Arity mismatch is deferred to the compatibility check.

rules.title: Associated/GAT types: covariant args, invariant GAT lifetime args
rules.statement: For an associated type projection (same trait_name and assoc_type_name): the base is covariant, each GAT type-arg is covariant, and each GAT lifetime-arg is invariant (must be equal; GAT lifetime variance is not user-controllable). Differing trait/name or arity is a shape difference.

rules.title: Inferred-type placeholder `_` is variance-compatible with any type
rules.statement: An InferredType (`_`) on either side of a structural-equality-with-lifetimes comparison is treated as a wildcard matching any type at any nesting depth (e.g. Vec<_> compares equal to Vec<i32>), letting region/type inference resolve it later.

rules.title: Empty lifetime acts as a wildcard in structural equality
rules.statement: In lifetime-aware structural equality, an empty (elided) lifetime on either side matches any lifetime (region inference resolves it). Otherwise lifetimes are equal iff syntactically identical, or mutually outliving ('a: 'b and 'b: 'a) which is treated as equality.

rules.title: Lifetime-aware structural equality is stronger than lifetime-erased TypeUID
rules.statement: Structural type equality used at invariant positions includes lifetime fragments and recurses through Ref/MutRef/Ptr (pointee + lifetime), Tuple/Array/Slice (elements), FnPtr/Closure (params + return), Struct/ZonedStruct/Enum (name, package, type-args, lifetime-args), and AssocType (trait, name, base, GAT type-args + lifetime-args). Two types differing only by an inner lifetime are unequal here even though TypeUID erases the lifetime. Primitives, TypeVars, and other kinds use TypeUID identity.

rules.title: Recursion depth cap conservatively accepts the subtype relation
rules.statement: If subtype recursion exceeds depth 64, or either operand is null, the relation is accepted (returns true), deferring soundness to the caller's separate compatibility check.
rules.uncertainty: Conservative termination guard, not a language-design choice.

rules.title: Per-position variance dictates the lifetime/type relation direction
rules.statement: At a position with variance v: Bivariant always holds; Covariant requires sub <: sup (lifetimes: 'sub: 'sup); Contravariant requires sup <: sub (lifetimes: 'sup: 'sub); Invariant requires equality (lifetime-aware structural equality for types; normalized-lifetime identity for lifetimes).
